Fixed: `![x\"x](x)` with `-x smarty` now gives `

`, the same as the unescaped version. Nothing is committed. **Cause:** a backslash-escaped character is replaced by a placeholder (its character code between two control characters) while Markdown parses. Those placeholders were only turned back into characters by `UnescapePostprocessor`, which runs on the final HTML string. By then the serializer had already escaped the attribute values, so the `"` went back in raw. Smarty adds `"` and `'` to the escapable characters, which is why it only showed up with that extension. **Fix** (`markdown/treeprocessors.py`): I added an `UnescapeTreeprocessor`, registered as `'unescape'` at priority 0 so it runs last. It puts the escaped characters back in every element's text, tail and attribute values *before* serialization, so the serializer escapes them properly. I left the old postprocessor registered because it still handles escapes inside stashed raw HTML, which isn't part of the element tree. **One visible side effect:** an escaped `>` (`\>`) now comes out as `>` instead of a raw `>`. Both are valid HTML, but the legacy fixture `tests/basic/backlash-escapes.html` expected the raw form, so I updated it. **Tests:** - New `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py` covering escaped quotes in plain text, inline and reference image alt text, and link titles. Three of these fail without the fix and pass with it. - An escaped-character alt-text test added to `tests/test_syntax/inline/test_images.py`. - I also added a note to the 3.4 release notes and updated the description of `unescape` in `docs/extensions/api.md`. **Test results:** 677 passed, 4 failed. The 4 failures are in `test_html_blocks.py` and fail the same way without my change; they look like Python 3.12 `HTMLParser` differences. `test_md_in_html.py` can't be collected by pytest in this setup (a collection warning gets treated as an error). I ran it with unittest instead, and it has 4 failures both with and without the change.
